abandon.definition: To stop doing, using or having something completely, especially suddenly or before it is finished.
abandon.example: Were the planners naive to expect drivers to abandon their cars within a single year?

abandoned.definition: Left behind and no longer used, lived in or cared for.
abandoned.example: An empty sack lay abandoned near the broken water tank.

abdicate.definition: To give up a position of power or responsibility.
abdicate.example: A leader who ignores pollution reports has quietly chosen to abdicate his duty to the community.

abrasive.definition: Something that is rough and can scratch; also describes a person whose manner is harsh.
abrasive.example: What was really behind that abrasive mask of his!

abruptly.example: Why did the livestream stop so abruptly just as the results were being announced?

absolutely.definition: Completely and totally, used to emphasise a strong feeling or statement.
absolutely.example: Nadir thought the speech about entrepreneurship was absolutely brilliant.

academy.definition: A school or college, often one that gives special training in a particular subject or skill.
academy.example: Next term the academy will introduce a robotics module for every Year Eight class.

accent.definition: A particular way of pronouncing words that shows which country, region or social group a person comes from.
accent.example: Constant teasing about his accent began to antagonise Sami, even though he hid it well.

accepted.definition: Agreed to take on something, such as blame or a duty, rather than avoiding or denying it.
accepted.example: Samira just got accepted into college!

accident.definition: An unexpected and unwanted event, often causing injury or damage, that happens without anyone intending it.
accident.example: The scar remained as a permanent reminder of the accident.

accidental.definition: Happening by chance rather than being planned or intended.
accidental.example: "Deliberate repetition is a drumbeat," our teacher said, "while accidental repetition is a stumble."

account.definition: A spoken or written report describing what happened in a particular situation or event.
account.example: A dependable witness gives the same account every time she is asked.

accountant's.definition: Belonging to an accountant, a person whose job is to keep, check and manage financial records.
accountant's.example: The accountant's integrity was tested when her manager asked her to hide the missing money.

accounting.definition: The profession or practice of recording, checking and reporting the financial activities of a person or organisation.
accounting.example: A recognised qualification in accounting opened doors that years of unrecorded experience could not.

accounts.definition: Spoken or written reports describing what happened, especially when given by different people about the same event.
accounts.example: Could a rumour really spread to millions of accounts in a single day?

accuracy.definition: The quality of being correct, exact and free from mistakes.
accuracy.example: I kept my resolution to practise free throws daily, and my accuracy slowly climbed all season.

accusation.definition: A statement claiming that someone has done something wrong or illegal.
accusation.example: Kofi frowned deeply at the unfair accusation.

accusations.definition: Statements claiming that someone has done something wrong, often made without solid proof.
accusations.example: Honestly, unfair accusations infuriate me more than any punishment a teacher could ever give.

achieve.definition: To succeed in doing or completing something, especially after effort.
achieve.example: Does ambition without discipline achieve anything, or does it simply remain a pleasant daydream?

achievement.definition: Something that has been accomplished through effort and skill.
achievement.example: What an achievement, thirty trees planted in a single morning!

achievements.definition: Things that a person has successfully done or gained through effort or skill.
achievements.example: A good biography describes both the struggles and the achievements of its subject.

acknowledge.definition: To accept or admit that something is true, or to recognise that you have received something.
acknowledge.example: Why is it sometimes so difficult to acknowledge a mistake in front of the whole class?

acoustic.definition: Relating to sound and the way it travels or is heard, especially inside a building or space.
acoustic.example: For years, the inexplicable echo in the tunnel puzzled every acoustic engineer who studied it.

acquire.definition: To get or gain something, usually by effort or learning.
acquire.example: Which digital skills should students acquire before they leave secondary school?

acrobats.definition: Performers who are trained to do difficult and impressive physical feats such as jumping, balancing and twisting.
acrobats.example: The agile acrobats leapt between the platforms while the festival crowd gasped below them.

act.definition: To do something, especially in order to deal with a situation, rather than simply thinking or talking about it.
act.example: Surely no true friend would act this way!

acted.definition: Performed a particular role or function, or behaved in a certain way.

activity.definition: Something that a person does, especially for interest, enjoyment or exercise.
activity.example: The workshop buzzed with activity, didn't it?

acts.definition: Serves in a particular role, or carries out a particular function.
acts.example: Small acts of kindness can change someone's entire day.

actual.definition: Real and existing, rather than imagined, expected or claimed.
actual.example: How often does online gossip match the actual reality of a situation?

actually.definition: In fact or in reality, especially when this is surprising or different from what was expected.
actually.example: Zane, that idea might actually work!

add.definition: To put something together with something else so that the total amount or number becomes greater.
add.example: Rohan, add your byline before you send the final draft!

added.definition: Put something extra together with what already existed, building on or increasing it.
added.example: The story developed slowly as each student added a new idea.

adding.definition: Putting something extra together with what already exists, so as to increase or improve it.
adding.example: The team solved the traffic problem by adding a new cycle lane.

adds.definition: Puts something extra together with what already exists, especially building on it over time.
adds.example: Every per cent of extra buying adds more waste to landfill.

adequate.definition: Good enough for what is needed; sufficient.
adequate.example: One shared laptop is hardly adequate for a family with three students studying at home.

adjust.definition: To change something slightly, especially to make it fit new conditions or work better.
adjust.example: "Passenger numbers fluctuate every season," the transport officer explained, "so we adjust the timetable twice a year."

adjusted.definition: Changed something slightly and carefully until it fitted or suited what was needed.
adjusted.example: Reading her capstone poem aloud, Maya adjusted the rhythm until every line matched her breathing.

adjusts.definition: Changes something, often automatically and continually, to suit new conditions.
adjusts.example: The city's sophisticated traffic system adjusts every signal using data from thousands of sensors.

admire.definition: To respect and think highly of someone or something because of their qualities or achievements.
admire.example: Many students write their biography about a grandparent they admire.

admiringly.definition: In a way that shows respect and approval for someone's qualities or achievements.
admiringly.example: "Our charismatic team leader convinced thirty volunteers to stay past midnight," reported Nora admiringly.

admitted.definition: Said something, often reluctantly, that was true but perhaps not easy or comfortable to state.
admitted.example: Ben admitted, "I've been rude to everyone lately!"

admitting.definition: Stating, often reluctantly, that something unwelcome or embarrassing is true.
admitting.example: Kofi earned Milo's respect by admitting his own mistakes.

admonish.definition: To tell someone firmly that they have done something wrong, often in a caring way.
admonish.example: Did the coach admonish the team for taking a shortcut across the protected dunes?

admonished.definition: Told someone firmly and seriously that they had done something wrong.
admonished.example: I felt embarrassed when the guide admonished me, yet I knew straying from the path was wrong.

adults.definition: Fully grown people, as opposed to children.
adults.example: Why does accountability matter more to adults than to students, Sir?

advance.definition: To develop, improve or move forward over time.
advance.example: Which profession do you believe will change most as technology continues to advance?

advanced.definition: At a higher level of skill or difficulty, beyond the basic or ordinary stage.
advanced.example: Every advanced skill in coding grows out of a few basic ideas.

adventure.definition: An exciting, unusual or sometimes risky experience or journey.
adventure.example: Travellers sometimes embellish their adventure stories until a gentle hill becomes a towering mountain.

adventurers.definition: People who enjoy seeking out exciting, unusual or risky experiences.
adventurers.example: Would an intrepid traveller enjoy our town's festival, or is it too calm for adventurers?

adventures.definition: Exciting or unusual experiences, often involving an element of risk or the unknown.
adventures.example: I found the elderly storyteller utterly charming, though I suspect he invented half his adventures.

advert's.definition: Belonging to an advert, a public notice or announcement promoting a product or service.
advert's.example: The advert's claim that the phone battery lasts three days collapsed under the reviewers' testing.

advertise.definition: To make something known publicly, especially in order to promote or draw attention to it.
advertise.example: Does an ostentatious station entrance welcome travellers, or does it simply advertise the architect?

advertisement.definition: A public notice, image or message designed to promote a product, service or event.
advertisement.example: The flashy advertisement promised more than it could deliver.

advertisements.definition: Public notices, images or messages designed to promote products, services or events.
advertisements.example: I now perceive advertisements very differently since our lesson on hidden persuasive techniques.

advertisers.definition: People or companies that pay to promote their products or services to the public.
advertisers.example: Advertisers know the connotation of the word new, so they print it in bold letters.

advertising.definition: The business or activity of creating public messages that promote products, services or events.
advertising.example: Can alliteration make an advertising slogan memorable without making it sound childish?

adverts.definition: Public notices, images or messages designed to promote products or services.
adverts.example: My opinion of the app changed abruptly after it filled my screen with untrustworthy adverts.

advice.definition: Guidance or recommendations given to someone about what they should do.
advice.example: Rohan learned to write concisely after his editor's advice.

advised.definition: Gave someone guidance or a suggestion about what they should do.
advised.example: "Choose one method and stay with it," Teacher Yasmin advised the class.

adviser.definition: A person whose job is to give expert guidance or recommendations to someone else.
adviser.example: The interview ended abruptly when the minister's adviser whispered something urgent in his ear.

affect.definition: To influence or cause a change in someone or something.
affect.example: How does logging affect the balance of a forest ecosystem?

affecting.definition: Influencing or beginning to cause a change in someone or something.
affecting.example: Was the champion's defeat inevitable once the injury started affecting her landing?

affiliation.definition: A connection or relationship with a group or organisation.
affiliation.example: "State your club affiliation on the form," said the official, "or your result will not count."

affordable.definition: Not too expensive, so that ordinary people are able to buy or pay for it.
affordable.example: I am wary of grand promises about new developments until I see plans for affordable housing.

afternoon.definition: The part of the day between midday and evening.
afternoon.example: Why is the sky darkening so quickly this afternoon?

afterwards.definition: After a particular event, at a later time.
afterwards.example: Maybe the boy who damaged the football regretted it afterwards?

against.definition: In opposition to a person, group or idea.
against.example: The wind pushed against the door with tremendous force.

age.definition: The length of time that a person has lived or a thing has existed.
age.example: The bicycle was still in good condition despite its age.

ageing.definition: Becoming old, or showing the effects of getting older.
ageing.example: Zane's wireless project accidentally overloaded the lab's ageing router.

agile.definition: Able to move quickly and easily.
agile.example: The agile acrobats leapt between the platforms while the festival crowd gasped below them.

agitate.definition: To make someone feel worried or upset.
agitate.example: Why does the flashing update icon agitate some users while others barely notice it?

agreed.definition: Said yes to doing something, or accepted a proposal or arrangement.
agreed.example: Everyone agreed it's better to talk than to fight.

agreement.definition: A shared opinion or decision reached by two or more people or groups.
agreement.example: Everyone at the table nodded in agreement once Ayeeyo finished her story.

aid.definition: Help given to someone, especially practical help such as medical treatment in an emergency.
aid.example: Passing my first-aid course felt like a real milestone on my path towards studying medicine.

aider.definition: A person trained to give emergency medical help to someone who is injured or unwell.
aider.example: 'Warm soup will alleviate the shivering,' said the first-aider, wrapping a blanket around the soaked hiker.

aiming.definition: Trying hard to achieve or reach a particular goal.
aiming.example: I am aiming for a distinction in my Arabic course, so I revise a little every evening after supper.

aimlessly.definition: Without any clear purpose, direction or plan.
aimlessly.example: "Plan the structure before you write," insisted Teacher Yasmin, "or your argument will wander aimlessly."

airtime.definition: The amount of time given to a particular subject or item on radio or television.
airtime.example: The station decided to allocate more airtime to local stories after listeners complained.

alarm.definition: A device that makes a loud noise to warn people of danger or to attract attention.
alarm.example: A loud alarm rang through the empty college corridor.

alarming.definition: Causing worry, fear or a feeling that something needs urgent attention.
alarming.example: That story tries far too hard to sound alarming, Milo said!

alerts.definition: Short messages sent to warn or inform people quickly about something happening.
alerts.example: Constant breaking-news alerts can agitate readers, leaving them anxious long after the screen goes dark.

alienate.definition: To make someone feel like they don't belong or are not part of a group.
alienate.example: Private jokes at the lunch table can quietly alienate the newcomer who longs to belong.

alike.definition: In the same way, used to show that something applies equally to two or more groups.
alike.example: Why does the unexplained signal from deep space intrigue scientists and students alike?

allege.definition: To say that something is true, but not prove it yet.
allege.example: Several websites allege that the company hid the security flaw for months before admitting it.

alleges.definition: Claims that something is true, especially something wrong or illegal, without yet proving it.
alleges.example:
"But an anonymous teacher alleges that students in Form 3 have skipped duty before."
"That's a claim," Zara said.

alleviate.definition: To make something less serious or easier to deal with.
alleviate.example: What can one school realistically do to alleviate the litter problem on the local beach?

alliteration.definition: The repetition of the same sound at the beginning of several words in a sentence or phrase.
alliteration.example: I enjoy hunting for alliteration in shop signs whenever we walk through the market.

allocate.definition: To give something to someone for a specific purpose.
allocate.example: The station decided to allocate more airtime to local stories after listeners complained.

allowed.definition: Gave permission for something to happen, or made it possible for something to happen.
allowed.example: Who is allowed to carry the ceremonial drum this year?

allows.definition: Gives permission for something, or makes it possible for something to happen.
allows.example: Is a website negligent if it allows false medical advice to circulate unchecked?

alone.definition: By itself or on its own, without anyone or anything else being involved or added.
alone.example: That mosquito would not leave me alone all evening!

alongside.definition: Next to or together with something else.
alongside.example: The kiosk sold mint gum alongside sweets and biscuits.

aloud.definition: In a voice loud enough to be heard, rather than silently or inside your head.
aloud.example: Kian asked the secretary to read the notes aloud again.

also.definition: In addition to something already mentioned; as well.
also.example: Does your brother also attend this school, Omar?

alter.definition: To change something, usually in a small but noticeable way.
alter.example: How does changing a single syllable alter the rhythm of an otherwise finished line?

alternative.example: Is there a realistic alternative to expensive new stadiums for cities that host the Games?

alternatives.definition: Other things that can be chosen instead of something else; different options.
alternatives.example: "We cannot impose our taste on customers," admitted the designer, "we can only offer alternatives."

ambition.definition: A strong desire to achieve something important in life.
ambition.example: Teacher Yasmin has always been supportive of every student's ambition.

ambitious.definition: Needing a great deal of effort, determination and skill to achieve, because it is large or difficult.
ambitious.example: What an ambitious series Ivy had planned for the whole school year!

amendment.definition: A change or addition to a law or document.
amendment.example: They agreed on writing a formal letter requesting an amendment to the rule.

among.definition: Surrounded by, or in the middle of, a group of people or things.
among.example: Was the duty rotated fairly among all the forms last term?

amounts.definition: Quantities of something, especially referring to how much of it there is.
amounts.example: The fast fashion cycle wastes huge amounts of water and energy.

analogy.definition: A way of explaining something by comparing it to something else that is similar.
analogy.example: Teacher Yasmin used the iceberg as an analogy for hidden hard work.

analyst.definition: A person whose job is to examine information in detail in order to give an expert opinion.
analyst.example: 'These figures indicate a serious problem,' said the analyst, pointing at the audience graph.

analyst's.definition: Belonging to an analyst, a person whose job is to examine information in detail to give an expert opinion.
analyst's.example: The analyst's prediction that natural fabrics would return to fashion proved accurate within two years.

ancestors.definition: Family members who lived a long time before a person, from whom that person is descended.
ancestors.example: Ayeeyo taught Alina to recite the names of her ancestors.

anger.definition: A strong feeling of displeasure or hostility towards someone or something.
anger.example: Did his anger cool once Kofi apologised?

angry.definition: Feeling or showing strong displeasure or annoyance.
angry.example: Rohan drafted a calm reply instead of an angry one.

animal.definition: A living creature that can move on its own and needs food to survive, especially one that is not a human being.
animal.example: Every animal in the yard bolted when the fence collapsed.

animals.definition: Living creatures that can move on their own and need food to survive, especially ones that are not human beings.
animals.example: The Boni Forest is home to rare animals and hundreds of plant species.

animosity.definition: A strong feeling of dislike or hatred towards someone.
animosity.example: How did such deep animosity grow between neighbours who once shared meals during every celebration?

ankle.definition: The joint that connects the foot to the leg.
ankle.example: "Swimming is an excellent alternative," the physiotherapist said, "while your ankle finishes healing."

anniversary.definition: The date each year on which people remember or celebrate something that happened in a previous year.
anniversary.example: Congratulations on the publication's tenth anniversary, Teacher Yasmin!

announced.definition: Said something officially or publicly, so that people would know about it.
announced.example: The girl waited quietly for the results to be announced.

announcements.definition: Public statements that give people information about something.
announcements.example: How can drivers remain oblivious to the new crossing signals after months of announcements?

announcing.definition: Stating something officially or publicly so that people are informed.
announcing.example: The judicial panel reviewed the disputed race footage before announcing its final decision.

annoying.definition: Causing mild anger, irritation or impatience.
annoying.example: Does repetition of the phrase 'buy less, choose well' make the campaign stronger or annoying?

anonymous.definition: With a name that is not known, given or made public.
anonymous.example: Is an anonymous account ever as reliable as an official government page?

another.definition: One more, or a different one, in addition to the one already mentioned.
another.example: This chapati is delicious, Amal — can I have another?

answer.definition: To respond to a question, criticism or situation, especially by giving information or reacting to it.
answer.example: A smart answer does not always mean a kind one.

answered.definition: Responded to something, such as a question or a message.
answered.example: The phone rang three times before Amal answered it!

answers.definition: Replies or responses given to questions, problems or objections.
answers.example: A strong defence answers the hardest question first, not last.

antagonise.definition: To make someone angry or upset by opposing them or being mean.
antagonise.example: Constant teasing about his accent began to antagonise Sami, even though he hid it well.

antenna.definition: A metal rod, wire or dish used to send or receive radio, television or other signals.
antenna.example: Who is that engineer sitting astride the steel beam, checking the antenna cables?

anthology.definition: A collection of poems, stories or other pieces of writing, gathered together and published as one book.
anthology.example: Every text in the anthology connects back to this year's capstone theme.

anthology's.definition: Belonging to an anthology, a published collection of poems, stories or other writing.
anthology's.example: Sami's perseverance through seven drafts turned a rejected story into the anthology's closing piece.

antique.definition: Old, and often valuable because it was made a long time ago.
antique.example: How can visitors tell an authentic antique lamp from the clever copies sold nearby?

anyone.definition: Any person at all, used especially in questions or negative sentences.
anyone.example: Can you name anyone in your own ancestry, Nora?

anyone's.definition: Belonging to any person at all.
anyone's.example: Sana wrote that a lonely flute could make anyone's heart shiver.

anything.definition: Any thing at all, used especially in questions, negative sentences or general statements.
anything.example: Why do you keep nodding without saying anything, Nora?

anyway.definition: Despite what has just been said or done; regardless of other factors.
anyway.example: Kofi ignored the doubters and kept improving the sensor design anyway.

apart.definition: Except for, or in addition to, something already mentioned.
apart.example: Has the seam already been taken apart, Maya?

apologies.definition: Statements telling someone that you are sorry for something you have done wrong.
apologies.example: I believe most conflict at home starts small and grows only because apologies come too late.

app.definition: A computer program, especially a small one designed to run on a smartphone or tablet.
app.example: Imani, the app shows humidity levels updating every few minutes.

appeal.definition: An urgent public request for help, money or support.
appeal.example: During the festival appeal, which benevolent gesture impressed you most, the donations or the volunteers' time?

appear.definition: To be seen, noticed or present in something, such as a piece of writing.
appear.example: Which month does the harvest festival appear on the calendar?

appears.definition: Is present, or can be found, in a particular place.
appears.example: Our final anthology includes one poem where the rhyme appears only in the first and last stanzas.

applauding.definition: Clapping the hands together to show approval or appreciation.
applauding.example: "What a charming welcome song," said the visiting mayor, applauding the youngest choir warmly.

applause.definition: The sound of many people clapping their hands together to show approval or appreciation.
applause.example: "A benevolent heart gives quietly," said the teacher, "seeking no applause from the crowd."

applicants.definition: People who formally apply for something, such as a job, course or scholarship.
applicants.example: What must applicants demonstrate to win the engineering scholarship offered by the city council?

application.definition: A formal, usually written, request for something such as a job, course or place.
application.example: "Experience matters," said the recruiter, "but without the right qualification your application stops at the first desk."

applications.definition: Formal, usually written, requests for something such as a place at university or a job.
applications.example: How can schools provide mentorship for pupils whose families know little about university applications?

appointed.definition: Chose someone officially for a particular job or role.
appointed.example: The hospital appointed a liaison to keep journalists informed without disturbing the medical teams.

appointments.definition: Arranged times at which someone will meet another person or receive a service.
appointments.example: The new booking system lets parents reserve appointments with remarkable ease from any device.

apprentice.definition: A person learning a trade or skill from an experienced worker.
apprentice.example: What willingness the young apprentice showed on his very first day!

apprenticeship.definition: A period of time spent working for an employer while learning a trade or skilled job.
apprenticeship.example: Tariq's apprenticeship gave him an opportunity he never expected.

approach.definition: To begin to deal with, think about or handle a task, problem or subject in a particular way.
approach.example: Farmers watch the sky closely as the rains approach each year.

approached.definition: Moved nearer to someone or something.
approached.example: Smoke from the bonfires smelled fragrant as evening approached.

approaching.definition: Moving nearer to something, or coming closer in time.
approaching.example: I promised to inform the group immediately if the weather app showed lightning approaching the ridge.

approved.definition: Officially agreed to, accepted or gave permission for a plan or proposal.
approved.example: The county office approved new funding for rural classrooms.

apps.definition: Computer programs, especially small ones designed to run on smartphones or tablets.
apps.example: I try not to compare my beginner projects with the polished apps that older students build.

archery.definition: The sport or skill of shooting arrows at a target using a bow.
archery.example: I enjoy the contrast between noisy team sports and the calm concentration of archery practice.

architects.definition: People whose job is to design buildings and oversee their construction.
architects.example: The architects promised to incorporate green roofs and rain gardens into the new sports hall design.

archive.definition: A collection of historical documents or records, kept and organised in one place.
archive.example: Sami wanted to explore the archive for older articles on the topic.

archway.definition: A curved structure, often forming an entrance or passageway.
archway.example: Which decoration took the longest to make: the star mobiles or the woven archway?

area.definition: A particular part of a place, town or region.
area.example: New saplings help a cleared area recover more quickly.

areas.definition: Particular parts of a place or region.
areas.example: One of the most exciting areas of change is future farming — using technology to grow more food with fewer resources.

argue.definition: To talk about something in a way that shows you have different opinions and want to convince someone.
argue.example: Regular debate practice will sharpen your ability to argue with evidence.

argued.definition: Gave reasons to support an opinion or claim, especially in order to persuade others.
argued.example: The petition argued that the rota had become unjust over time.

argument.definition: A discussion where people express different opinions about something.
argument.example: Where is the logic in that argument, Sami?

argumentative.definition: Someone who likes to argue or disagree with others.
argumentative.example: Is being argumentative a flaw in friendship but a strength in formal debate?

arguments.definition: Reasons given to support or oppose an idea, especially in order to persuade someone.
arguments.example: Old arguments between the two boys sometimes flared up again.

army.definition: A large organised group of soldiers trained to fight on land.
army.example: The old diary described the invading general's malevolence towards every village that resisted his army.

arranged.definition: Organised or planned something in advance, or put things in a particular order.
arranged.example: The shopkeeper arranged the items neatly on the wooden shelf.

arrival.definition: The act of arriving, or coming to a particular place.
arrival.example: How long had the town awaited the arrival of the Great Drum?

arrived.definition: Reached a place, or came about after being expected or worked towards.
arrived.example: Finally, the holiday has arrived, Maya!

arrows.definition: Symbols shaped like a straight line with a pointed head at one end, used to show direction.
arrows.example: The coach drew arrows on the whiteboard to illustrate how the winger should cut inside.

art.definition: Creative work such as painting, drawing or sculpture, made to be looked at and appreciated.
art.example: How many blank sheets do you need for the art project?

article's.definition: Belonging to an article, a piece of writing published in a newspaper, magazine or online.
article's.example: A missing byline made the article's author impossible to trace.

articles.definition: Pieces of writing published in a newspaper, magazine or website.
articles.example: Sami wanted to explore the archive for older articles on the topic.

artists.definition: People who create art, such as paintings, drawings or sculptures.
artists.example: Artists often paint the sky in colours nobody else notices.

ashamed.definition: Feeling guilty, embarrassed or sorry because of something you have done.
ashamed.example: Keep standing, Amal, you have nothing to be ashamed of!

aside.definition: To one side, or away from the main position, especially so as to be dealt with later or ignored.
aside.example: "Commentators must set aside personal bias," explained the editor, "or viewers will stop trusting the coverage."

asked.definition: Put a question to someone, or requested that someone do something.
asked.example: "What's going on between you two?" Kofi asked calmly.

askew.definition: Not straight or level; tilted to one side.
askew.example: Why has that station clock hung askew for months without anyone repairing it?

asking.definition: Requesting something, or putting a question to someone.
asking.example: There is no shame, Sami, in asking for help!

asks.definition: requires or requests that someone do a particular thing.
asks.example: Why do your eyes keep shifting when Kofi asks a question?

aspiration.definition: A hope or dream of achieving something in the future.
aspiration.example: Does every aspiration need a deadline, or can some dreams stay open-ended?

assembly.definition: a gathering of a school's students and teachers, usually for announcements or a shared activity.
assembly.example: Which club hosted the assembly this term, Sami?

assertion.definition: A strong statement that something is true.
assertion.example: Has a phrase ever stuck in your mind the way Zane's assertion did?

assignment.definition: a piece of work given to a student to complete, often as part of a course.
assignment.example: The teacher warned the class that plagiarising an essay would fail the assignment.

assured.definition: told someone firmly and confidently that something was true, to stop them worrying.
assured.example: "Feeling vulnerable on stage is normal," the drama coach assured us before the capstone reading.

astride.definition: With one leg on each side of something.
astride.example: Who is that engineer sitting astride the steel beam, checking the antenna cables?

athlete.definition: a person who is trained in and takes part in sport, especially running, jumping or similar events.
athlete.example: Is the man by the gate really a former Olympic athlete?

athlete's.definition: belonging to a person who is trained in and competes in sport.
athlete's.example: What substances are tested for in an athlete's blood sample, Idris?

athletes.definition: people who are trained in and take part in sport, especially running, jumping or similar events.
athletes.example: Officials banned two athletes after they failed the drugs test.

athletes'.definition: belonging to a group of people who are trained in and compete in sport.

community.definition: a group of people who live in the same area, or who share something in common.

commuter.definition: a person who regularly travels a distance to work, often using public transport.

commuters.definition: people who regularly travel a distance to work, often using public transport.

companies.definition: businesses that produce or sell goods and services.

company.definition: a business that produces or sells goods and services.

company's.definition: belonging to a business that produces or sells goods and services.

compare.definition: To look at two or more things to see how they are similar or different.

compared.definition: looked at two or more things together to see how they are similar or different.

comparison.definition: the act of looking at two or more things together to see how they are similar or different.

compass.definition: a small device with a needle that always points north, used to find direction.

compassion.definition: a strong feeling of sympathy and care for someone who is suffering.

competition.definition: an event in which people try to win by being the best at something.

competitions.definition: events in which people try to win by being the best at something.

competitor.definition: a person who takes part in a contest, race or match, trying to win.

complacent.definition: Feeling satisfied with yourself and not wanting to improve or change.

complaint.definition: a statement that expresses someone's dissatisfaction about something.

complaints.definition: statements that express dissatisfaction about something.

completely.definition: totally, in every way; not partly.

complicated.definition: having many different parts, and so difficult to understand or deal with.

component.definition: A part or piece of something larger.

computer.definition: an electronic machine that can store, process and use information.

computers.definition: electronic machines that can store, process and use information.

computing.definition: the use and study of computers and the writing of programs for them.

conceive.definition: To think of or create an idea or plan in your mind.

conceived.definition: thought of and formed an idea or plan in the mind.

concentrate.definition: to give all of one's attention and thought to a single task.
concentrate.example: Students who sleep enough usually concentrate better in class.

concentration.definition: the ability to give all of one's attention and thought to a single task.

concept.definition: a basic idea or principle that something else is built on.

concerns.definition: worries or matters that cause someone to feel uneasy.

concert.example: The school built a new outdoor stage for the spring concert.

concluded.definition: decided or worked out a final result, after considering the evidence.

concrete.definition: a hard building material made from cement, sand, water and small stones.

conditions.definition: the circumstances in which people live or work, especially how comfortable or safe things are.
conditions.example: Which point should our presentation emphasise first: the water cost or the workers' conditions?

conference.definition: a large meeting, often lasting more than one day, where people discuss a particular subject.

confess.definition: to admit that you have done something wrong, or that something you were hiding is true.

confessed.definition: admitted that something was true, especially something previously hidden or uncertain.

confessing.definition: admitting that something is true, especially something previously hidden.

confidence.definition: The feeling of believing in yourself and your abilities.
confidence.example: She envied the quiet confidence of her older cousin.

confident.definition: feeling sure of one's own abilities, or sure that something is true.

confidently.definition: in a way that shows a sure, positive belief in oneself or in something.

confirmed.definition: stated that something was definitely true or genuine.

conflict.definition: A disagreement or fight between people or groups.

confusing.definition: difficult to understand, and likely to make someone feel unsure or muddled.

confusion.definition: a state of not understanding something clearly, or of being unsure about it.
confusion.example: Yelling in the corridor only made the confusion worse.

congestion.definition: a state in which roads or areas are too crowded with traffic or people, causing delays.
congestion.example: It would be naive to believe one new bus route could solve the whole district's congestion.

connect.definition: to join or link two or more things together.

connecting.definition: joining or linking two or more things together.

connects.definition: joins or links two or more things together.

connive.definition: To secretly plan to do something wrong or illegal with someone else.

connotation.definition: The feelings or ideas that a word makes you think of, beyond its basic meaning.
connotation.example: Advertisers know the connotation of the word new, so they print it in bold letters.

conscious.definition: Aware of and able to think about what is happening.

consecutive.definition: Happening one after another without any breaks.

consequences.definition: the results or effects that follow from an action, especially unwanted ones.
consequences.example: Cheating in an exam can lead to serious consequences for a student.

conservation.definition: the protection and careful management of nature, wildlife or historic places.

consider.definition: to think carefully about something before forming an opinion or making a decision.

considered.definition: was thought of, or regarded, in a particular way.

constant.definition: happening all the time, without stopping.

construction.definition: the process or work of building something.

consult.definition: To ask someone for advice or information.

contemporary.definition: Living or happening at the same time; modern.

content.definition: the information, ideas or material contained within something, such as a website or speech, rather than its style.
content.example: Which amendment to the media law finally required websites to label sponsored content?

context.definition: The situation or background that helps you understand something.
context.example: Why is context so important when journalists quote an athlete's angry comments after a defeat?

continents.definition: the very large areas of land that the Earth's surface is divided into, such as Africa or Asia.
continents.example: Long tables sagged under the harvest feast, where dishes from four continents sat side by side.

continues.definition: keeps happening or going on without stopping.

contracts.definition: formal written agreements between two or more people or organisations that can be enforced by law.

contradict.definition: to say the opposite of what someone else has said, or to disagree with a set of facts.

contrast.definition: The difference between two things when you compare them.
contrast.example: What contrast do you notice between the ancient Games and the modern Olympic ceremonies?

contrasted.definition: compared two things by pointing out how different they are.

contrasting.definition: showing clear differences when compared with something else.

contribute.definition: To give something, like help or ideas, to a common purpose.

contribution.definition: Something you give or do to help achieve something or to help others.

control.definition: the power to direct or manage how something behaves or is used.

controversial.definition: likely to cause strong disagreement, because people hold very different opinions about it.

convenience.definition: the quality of being easy and helpful to use, without much effort.

converge.definition: To come together from different directions to meet at one point.

conversation.definition: a talk between two or more people in which they exchange ideas or information.

convey.definition: To communicate or express a message, feeling or idea.

convince.definition: To persuade someone to believe or do something.

convinced.definition: made someone believe that something was true, or persuaded them to do something.

cooking.definition: the activity of preparing and heating food to make it ready to eat.

council.definition: a group of people elected or appointed to govern and make decisions for a town, city or area.

counts.definition: is regarded as valuable, acceptable, or belonging to a particular category.

coverage.definition: the reporting of an event or subject by the news media.

crops.definition: plants grown in large amounts, especially for food, and gathered at harvest time.

crowded.definition: very full of people, so that there is little space.

crowds.definition: large groups of people gathered together in one place.

crude.definition: Not finished or made in a simple and rough way.

cruel.definition: causing pain or suffering to others deliberately, without care for their feelings.

crush.definition: a large number of people pressed tightly together in a small space.

cuffs.definition: the ends of the sleeves of a piece of clothing, around the wrist.

cultures.definition: the shared customs, beliefs, arts and ways of life of particular groups of people.

curiosity.definition: a strong desire to know or learn about something.

customers.definition: people who buy goods or services from a shop or business.

customers'.definition: belonging to people who buy goods or services from a shop or business.

dam.example: The dam is releasing extra water after the heavy rain.

damage.definition: harm or injury done to something, making it less good, useful or valuable.

damaged.definition: harmed or spoiled, so that something is less good, useful or valuable than before.

dance.definition: to move the body rhythmically, usually in time with music.

dare.definition: to be brave enough to do something risky or difficult.

daring.definition: being brave enough to do something risky.

darkened.definition: became darker, especially as night approached.

darkest.definition: having the least light; most dark.

dashboard.definition: a screen or panel that displays information, such as data or controls, for a system or vehicle.

data.definition: facts and information, especially in the form of numbers, used for analysis or reference.
data.example: Amal collected data about the birds she saw along the river.

dates.definition: the sweet, sticky, brown fruits of the date palm tree, often eaten dried.
dates.example: Ayeeyo helped Alina fill her chronicle with names and dates.

dating.definition: existing since, or belonging to, a particular time in the past.
dating.example: The librarians helped the students organise the archive of school newspapers dating back forty years.

dawn.definition: the time of day when light first appears in the sky, just before sunrise.
dawn.example: We are heading north at dawn, Sami!

daydream.definition: a pleasant series of thoughts about things a person would like to happen, imagined while awake.
daydream.example: "Ambition without a plan is only a daydream," Teacher Yasmin told the careers assembly.

days.definition: periods of twenty-four hours, or the parts of that time when it is light.
days.example: Are you counting the days until the festival starts?

dazzling.definition: extremely impressive or bright, in a way that amazes people.
dazzling.example: I prefer one authentic tradition, honestly explained, to ten dazzling performances invented for tourists.

deadline.definition: a time or date by which something must be finished.

debate.definition: a formal discussion in which people express different opinions about a subject.

debates.definition: formal discussions in which people express different opinions about a subject.

debating.example: "You are argumentative today," laughed Leo, "so you should definitely join the debating society."

debugging.definition: the process of finding and fixing mistakes in a computer program.

decades.example: Local farmers are working to reverse decades of deforestation.

deceitful.definition: Someone who lies or tricks others.

decide.definition: to choose something after thinking about the possibilities.

decided.definition: chose something after thinking about the possibilities.

decision.definition: a choice made after thinking about the possibilities.
