tutoring.example: More students became industrious, organising events, tutoring, and contributing to school improvement.

twice.example: Sami trains twice a week at the local wrestling club.

type.definition: printed or displayed letters and characters, especially considered in terms of their size or style.
type.example: Why do headlines often allege wrongdoing loudly, then print their corrections in the smallest type?

typed.definition: written using a keyboard rather than by hand.
typed.example: My handwriting grows worse every year, which is my favourite argument for typed homework.

typing.definition: the action of writing text using a keyboard.
typing.example: After a two-week lapse in practice, my typing speed dropped by ten words per minute.

uncharged.definition: not given electrical power; not filled with the energy needed to work.
uncharged.example: 'Devices left uncharged overnight are liable to fail during the exam,' warned the invigilator.

unchecked.definition: not stopped, controlled or examined; allowed to continue freely.
unchecked.example: Is a website negligent if it allows false medical advice to circulate unchecked?

uncle.definition: the brother of your mother or father, or the husband of your aunt.
uncle.example: My uncle has worked at the port for over ten years.

underestimate.definition: to think that something is smaller, less important or less powerful than it actually is.
underestimate.example: "Never underestimate the influence of a headline," the editor said, "because most people read nothing else."

underfunding.definition: a situation in which not enough money is provided for something to work properly.
underfunding.example: The investigation exposed chronic underfunding in the region's rural internet infrastructure.

underline.definition: to draw a line beneath a word or phrase to give it emphasis.
underline.example: I underline sparingly in my essays now, choosing to emphasise only the argument that matters most.

underpass.definition: a path or road that goes underneath another road or railway.
underpass.example: Commuters remain wary of the shortcut through the underpass since the lighting failed last month.

understand.definition: to know the meaning of something or how it works.
understand.example: Alina wanted to understand her own culture more deeply.

underwater.definition: existing, happening or used below the surface of water.
underwater.example: Look at that coral, Amal, it's like an underwater garden!

uneven.example: "I would characterise this fabric as forgiving," said the tailor, "it hides a beginner's uneven stitches."

unexplained.definition: not made clear or given a reason for; mysterious.
unexplained.example: Why does an unexplained absence always become a canvas for gossip?

unfair.definition: not treating people equally or justly; not right or reasonable.
unfair.example: Kofi frowned deeply at the unfair accusation.

unfairly.definition: in a way that treats people unequally or unjustly.
unfairly.example: Milo felt he was punished unfairly after the fight.

unfinished.example: Unfinished endings infuriate some readers, yet our class anthology deliberately left two stories open.

unforgettable.definition: so special, unusual or impressive that it stays in your memory.
unforgettable.example: What an unforgettable event that turned out to be!

uniforms.definition: sets of identical clothes worn by members of an organisation, such as a school.
uniforms.example: Pupils exchange old uniforms for ones that still fit.

unit.definition: a section of a course of study that focuses on a particular topic.
unit.example: This unit ends with a biography of someone in your own family.

united.definition: joined together and acting as one; not divided.
united.example: I think a boycott succeeds only when the community stays united and patient for months.

unity.definition: the state of being joined together as one, especially through shared feelings or aims.
unity.example: Why antagonise your teammates before the final match, when unity is what you need most?

university.definition: an institution of higher education where students study for degrees.
university.example: Some students hope to become doctors after finishing university.

unkindness.definition: behaviour that is unpleasant or cruel and lacking in care for others' feelings.
unkindness.example: I believe silence protects those who harass, which is why reporting unkindness takes real courage.

unless.definition: except if; only if something happens or is true.
unless.example: How can we empathise with elderly residents unless we walk through the busy station ourselves?

unlocked.definition: not fastened or made secure, so it can be opened freely.
unlocked.example: "Leaving the server room unlocked was negligent," said the technician, "not merely forgetful."

unmistakably.definition: in a way that is completely clear and cannot be confused with anything else.
unmistakably.example: The magazine's youngest columnist writes about sustainable fashion in a voice that is unmistakably her own.

unnamed.definition: not identified or made known publicly; kept anonymous.
unnamed.example: I find munificent giving most beautiful when the giver insists on remaining unnamed.

unread.definition: not yet looked at or gone through, as with a book or article.
unread.example: My chronic habit of leaving articles unread until Sunday means I am always the last to know.

unrecorded.definition: not written down or officially noted anywhere.
unrecorded.example: A recognised qualification in accounting opened doors that years of unrecorded experience could not.

unreliable.definition: not able to be trusted or depended on to work or behave as expected.
unreliable.example: Teacher Yasmin taught the class how to tell a reliable website from an unreliable one.

unrewarded.definition: not given any praise, payment or recognition for effort made.
unrewarded.example: Looking back, the most benevolent act I witnessed this year was quiet and completely unrewarded.

unsolved.definition: not yet explained or worked out.
unsolved.example: Stories about unsolved codes always intrigue me, especially the ciphers that have defeated computers.

unstable.definition: likely to change, move or fall; not firm or steady.
unstable.example: "Let's evaluate both routes carefully," said Maya, "since the shorter path crosses an unstable slope."

unsupervised.definition: done without anyone watching over or being in charge.
unsupervised.example: "Integrity means doing right when nobody is watching," Teacher Yasmin reminded us before the unsupervised test.

unswept.definition: left dirty or covered in dust because it has not been cleaned.
unswept.example: Her inference that the factory had closed came from the silent machines and unswept floor.

untangling.definition: separating or sorting out something that has become twisted or mixed together.
untangling.example: I consider myself tenacious, yet untangling three hundred metres of festival lights nearly defeated me.

untidy.definition: not neat or well arranged; messy.
untidy.example: Apparently the deputy head wanted to punish the whole class for being untidy.

untrustworthy.definition: not able to be relied on as honest or reliable.
untrustworthy.example: Why does careless punctuation make even a brilliant fashion article feel untrustworthy?

unveils.definition: shows or reveals something publicly for the first time.
unveils.example: Visitors jostle for position at the launch event whenever a famous inventor unveils a new device.

unverified.definition: not yet checked or confirmed to be true.
unverified.example: Every reader who refuses to pass on an unverified claim helps the whole community.

update.definition: a piece of new information that brings something up to date, or the act of doing this.
update.example: The school posted an update after the governor's surprise visit.

updated.definition: made more current or accurate by adding new information.
updated.example: The updated schedule shared the work fairly among every form.

updates.definition: pieces of new information added to keep something current.
updates.example: I follow every development in space exploration, reading the updates the moment I get home.

upgrades.definition: improvements made to something, such as new or better versions of equipment.
upgrades.example: How should the council allocate its small technology budget between laptops and internet upgrades?

ups.definition: in 'pop-ups', small windows or messages that appear suddenly on a screen, often without being requested.
ups.example: 'Pop-ups that flash urgent warnings are designed to bamboozle you,' the computing teacher explained calmly.

upset.definition: an unexpected result in a competition, especially when a stronger competitor is defeated by a weaker one.
upset.example: Rohan worried that the story might upset the head teacher.

upstairs.definition: to or on a higher floor of a building.
upstairs.example: "The lobby is rather ostentatious," murmured Maya, "while the platforms upstairs lack seating."

upstream.definition: in the direction against the flow of a river, towards its source.
upstream.example: Is there a significant risk of flooding if the wetlands upstream continue to disappear?

urged.definition: strongly encouraged or advised someone to do something.
urged.example: "Read it aloud and feel the rhythm," urged Adam, tapping the desk with his pencil.

urgency.definition: the quality of needing immediate attention or action.
urgency.example: Can you paraphrase the designer's argument without losing the urgency of her original words?

urgent.definition: needing to be dealt with immediately.
urgent.example: The captain summoned the whole team for an urgent meeting.

usage.definition: the way something is employed, or the total amount consumed or applied.
usage.example: "That assertion needs a source," noted the editor, circling the sentence about water usage.

use.definition: to employ something for a particular purpose.
use.example: Whose turn is it to use the mop today, Milo?

used.definition: employed something for a purpose, or, as in 'used to', did something regularly in the past but not any more.
used.example: What a quick temper he used to have!

useful.definition: helpful and able to serve a purpose effectively.
useful.example: What a useful net that turned out to be!

user.definition: a person who operates or works with something, especially a product, service or device.
user.example: "First determine what the user actually needs," said the designer, "then start sketching the screens."

users.definition: people who operate or work with something, especially a product, service or device.
users.example: The article was shared by millions of users, though hardly anyone had checked it.

uses.definition: employs something for a particular purpose.
uses.example: A true competitor never uses an unfair advantage to win.

using.definition: employing something as a tool or method to do something.
using.example: Amara suggested using solar energy instead of coal!

usually.example: What do you usually do at lunchtime, Leo?

utterly.example: "He cycled past his own stop, utterly oblivious," laughed Maya, "lost in his audiobook again."

vague.definition: not clearly or precisely expressed or defined.
vague.example: "Bring copious examples to the debate," advised the coach, "because vague claims convince nobody."

valley.definition: a long, low area of land between hills or mountains, often with a river running through it.
valley.example: A dark cloud settled over the valley just before the rain.

valuable.definition: worth a lot, either in money or in importance.
valuable.example: Ayeeyo often says a good story leaves something valuable behind.

value.definition: the importance, worth or usefulness of something, or to consider something important or worthwhile.
value.example: Why do employers value initiative so highly when they interview school leavers?

vandalism.definition: the deliberate destruction or damage of property.
vandalism.example: "This proposal is not frivolous," insisted Nora, "play spaces genuinely reduce vandalism."

vase.definition: a container, often decorative, used for holding cut flowers.

vast.definition: extremely large in area, size or amount.
vast.example: Zane's small vessels seemed tiny against the vast ocean.

vengeful.definition: Feeling a strong desire to hurt someone because they have hurt you.
vengeful.example: In my view, vengeful thoughts are like carrying hot coals that burn the carrier first.

venue.definition: the place where an event, such as a meeting or competition, takes place.
venue.example: When rain flooded the pitch, the coaches quickly arranged an alternative venue in the sports hall.

verdict.definition: a decision or judgement given about something, especially after careful consideration.
verdict.example: The reviewer's blunt verdict, though painful to read, saved the team months of wasted effort.

verified.definition: confirmed that something is true or accurate.
verified.example: The reporter protected her source but still verified every detail independently.

versatile.definition: Able to do many different things or adapt to many situations.
versatile.example: Which is more versatile for a young coder: a cheap laptop or a powerful tablet?

version.definition: a particular form of something that differs slightly from other forms of the same thing.
version.example: Who drafted the first version of the petition, Kian?

veteran.definition: a person with a great deal of experience in a particular activity, especially someone who has taken part for a long time.
veteran.example: What theme connects the stories of the refugee team and the veteran returning champion?

victories.definition: occasions of winning, especially in a contest or battle.
victories.example: "Resilience is built in the hard seasons," said the coach, "not in the easy victories."

victory.definition: the act of winning a battle, contest or struggle.
victory.example: The olive wreath became a lasting symbol of victory and honour.

video.definition: a recording of moving images, often with sound.
video.example: Who posted the video that everyone is talking about?

videos.definition: recordings of moving images, usually with sound.
videos.example: I appreciate my sister's blunt advice about my videos, even when it stings for an hour.

view.definition: a personal opinion about something, or the scene that can be seen from a particular place.
view.example: The front seat gives the best view of the road ahead.

viewer's.definition: belonging to a person who is watching something, such as a video or photo.
viewer's.example: I spent longer choosing the caption than editing the photo, because words steer the viewer's feelings.

viewers.definition: people who watch something, such as a television programme, video or event.
viewers.example: The documentary's careful evidence managed to convince even the most sceptical viewers.

viewpoint.definition: A way of thinking about something; a perspective.
viewpoint.example: How would the story of the final change if it were told from the goalkeeper's viewpoint?

vigilance.definition: careful and continuous attention paid in order to notice possible danger or problems.
vigilance.example: I think being lax about small repairs eventually costs a city far more than vigilance would.

vigilant.definition: Always watching carefully and ready to notice anything wrong or dangerous.
vigilant.example: "Be vigilant with the candles," warned the caretaker, "one gust could ruin months of work."

village's.definition: belonging to a small rural community.

villagers.definition: people who live in a small community in the countryside.
villagers.example: The villagers believed her promise, didn't they?

villages.definition: small communities of houses in the countryside, smaller than a town.
villages.example: The traders carried goods from the coast to villages inland.

villain.definition: the main bad character in a story, film or play.
villain.example: In my final essay, I contrasted the belligerent villain with the patient mentor who eventually changed him.

vindictive.definition: Wanting to hurt someone because they hurt you.
vindictive.example: Only someone as vindictive as Kofi would do this, Jamal thought.

visit.definition: to go to see a person or place for a period of time.
visit.example: Ben promised to visit Kofi again within a week.

visited.definition: went to see a person or place.
visited.example: Has the governor ever visited a school in your town?

visiting.definition: going to see a person or place, or, as an adjective, coming from elsewhere to be present somewhere for a short time.
visiting.example: The cooks prepared their finest dishes for the visiting elders.

visitor.definition: a person who comes to see or stay in a place for a short time.
visitor.example: The unexpected visitor arrived just as the assembly was ending.

visitors.definition: people who come to see or stay in a place for a short time.
visitors.example: Decorated roads welcomed visitors from every neighbouring town.

vivid.definition: producing very clear, powerful images in the mind; brightly coloured or intense.
vivid.example: Alina tried to describe her great-grandfather's boats in vivid detail.

vocabulary.definition: the set of words that a person knows or that belong to a particular language or subject.
vocabulary.example: Historians use precise words for these ways of remembering, and every one of them belongs in your capstone vocabulary.

vocation.definition: A strong feeling of being suited to a particular career or calling.
vocation.example: How do you know whether a career is merely work or a true vocation?

voice.definition: The sound that you make when you speak or sing; also, a writer's unique style.
voice.example: What a soft voice you have this morning, Nora!

voluntary.definition: done, given or carried out of one's own free will, without being forced or paid.
voluntary.example: Should the school impose a uniform recycling scheme, or should participation stay voluntary?

volunteer.definition: a person who offers to do something, especially unpaid work, without being forced, or to offer to do something willingly.
volunteer.example: She thanked every volunteer at the end of the event.

volunteering.definition: doing work, usually unpaid, to help other people or a cause, without being forced.
volunteering.example: Is volunteering along the river as rewarding as the ranger says it is?

volunteers.definition: people who offer to do something, especially unpaid work, without being forced.
volunteers.example: Volunteers spent the morning counting chairs for the ceremony.

volunteers'.definition: belonging to people who offer to do something without being forced or paid.
volunteers'.example: During the festival appeal, which benevolent gesture impressed you most, the donations or the volunteers' time?

vote.definition: to formally express a choice or opinion, especially by marking a paper or raising a hand.
vote.example: Lunchtime felt shorter than usual on the day of the vote.

vulnerable.definition: Able to be easily hurt or harmed, either physically or emotionally.
vulnerable.example: Why do the most vulnerable moments in a story often become the ones readers remember?

wait.definition: to stay in a place or delay an action until something happens or someone arrives.
wait.example: Sami couldn't wait to try the roasted mangoes at the fire!

waited.definition: stayed in a place or delayed an action until something happened.
waited.example: Ben kicked a stone across the yard while he waited.

waiting.definition: staying in a place or delaying an action until something happens.
waiting.example: Thank you, driver, for waiting for us!

waking.example: "I am enthusiastic about hosting the food fair," said Theo, "even though it means waking at dawn."

walking.definition: moving on foot at a normal pace.
walking.example: Walking near the cliff edge at night is dangerous.

wall.definition: an upright structure, usually made of brick or stone, that separates or encloses an area.
wall.example: Has anyone counted how many posters are on that wall?

wander.definition: to walk around slowly without a fixed direction or purpose, or, of an argument, to lose focus.
wander.example: "Plan the structure before you write," insisted Teacher Yasmin, "or your argument will wander aimlessly."

want.definition: to desire or wish for something.
want.example: Would you want fame if it meant losing your privacy?

wanted.example: Alina wanted to understand her own culture more deeply.

wants.example: Sami, the head teacher wants to see you after lunch!

war.definition: an armed conflict between countries or groups.
war.example: How does a single casualty in a small village change the way its people remember a war?

warden.definition: a person responsible for supervising or enforcing rules in a particular place, such as a park or campsite.
warden.example: The warden had to admonish two campers who left their fire smouldering beside the dry grass.

wardrobe.definition: a large cupboard for storing clothes, or, figuratively, a person's whole collection of clothes.
wardrobe.example: Buying a smaller quantity of clothes can still fill a whole wardrobe.

warily.definition: In a way that shows you are careful and do not trust something completely.
warily.example: Sami stepped warily into the abandoned courtyard where his grandfather's house had once stood.

warm.definition: having or giving out a comfortable level of heat, or, figuratively, friendly and affectionate.
warm.example: Why does cardamom tea have such a rich, warm smell?

warming.definition: becoming or making something hotter than before.
warming.example: Can you think of an analogy that explains why warming up matters before a sprint?

warmly.definition: in a friendly, enthusiastic or affectionate way.
warmly.example: "What a charming welcome song," said the visiting mayor, applauding the youngest choir warmly.

warmth.definition: a pleasant feeling of heat, or, figuratively, friendliness and affection.
warmth.example: Local customs differ from village to village, but the warmth behind them stays the same.

warned.definition: told someone about a possible danger or problem in advance.
warned.example: Jamal warned, "Save your tricks for someone else!"

warning.definition: a statement or sign that tells someone of a possible danger or problem.
warning.example: Ben screamed a warning the moment he saw the flames.

warnings.definition: statements or signs that tell someone of a possible danger or problem.
warnings.example: Sami thought he heard the sea whispering warnings before the storm.

wary.definition: Careful about possible dangers or problems.
wary.example: Why are some residents wary of driverless buses despite the encouraging safety statistics?

washed.definition: carried or moved by the action of water.
washed.example: Once the clothes are sorted, each pile is washed and measured.

waste.definition: unwanted material that is thrown away, or to use something carelessly without a useful result.
waste.example: Food waste can decompose within just a few weeks.

wasted.definition: used carelessly without gaining any benefit; spent without a useful result.
wasted.example: Sana liked how the essay ended without a single wasted word.

watch.definition: to look at something for a period of time, paying attention to it.
watch.example: Watch him, he's stormed off again!

watched.definition: looked at something for a period of time, paying attention to it.
watched.example: Kofi watched, confused, as Jamal stormed towards him.

watches.definition: looks at something for a period of time, paying attention to it.
watches.example: "These recipes will endure," promised Grandmother, "as long as one child watches me cook."

watching.definition: looking at something for a period of time, paying attention to it.
watching.example: How proud Ayeeyo felt watching her grandchild recite the family line!

waterproof.definition: designed to keep water out; not letting water through.
waterproof.example: I can only conclude, after three soggy nights, that my bargain tent was never truly waterproof.

waves.definition: moving ridges of water on the surface of the sea or another body of water.
waves.example: Waves battered the harbour wall until the storm finally passed.

way.definition: a method, manner or route for doing or reaching something.
way.example: What a long way they sailed, Sami!

ways.definition: different methods or routes for doing or achieving something.
ways.example: The customs of these two countries are remarkably similar in many ways.

weak.definition: lacking physical strength, power or effectiveness.
weak.example: I realised that a trembling start does not always predict a weak speech.

weakest.definition: having the least strength, power or effectiveness, compared to others.
weakest.example: 'The teardown will reveal the phone's weakest part,' the reviewer promised her curious viewers.

weakness.definition: a lack of strength, power or effectiveness, or a fault or shortcoming.
weakness.example: A willingness to ask for help is not a weakness, Teacher Yasmin often says.

wearing.definition: having clothes or an item on your body.
wearing.example: Kofi, that is a very flashy jacket you are wearing!

weave.definition: to make cloth or a basket by crossing threads or strips over and under each other, or, figuratively, to combine different elements into a whole.
weave.example: How long does it take to weave a basket from straw?

weaving.definition: making cloth, baskets or similar objects by crossing threads or strips over and under each other.
weaving.example: Imani watched attentively as the elder demonstrated the ancient weaving technique.

website.definition: a set of related pages on the internet, usually about a particular subject or organisation.
website.example: When exactly was the video first uploaded to the school website?

website's.definition: belonging to a particular set of internet pages.
website's.example: How can we determine whether a website's statistics deserve our trust?

websites.definition: sets of related pages on the internet, usually about a particular subject or organisation.
websites.example: The team researched the topic using only official government websites.

weekend.definition: Saturday and Sunday, the days when most people do not work.
weekend.example: How big was the crowd at the weekend match?

weekend's.definition: belonging to Saturday and Sunday, the days when most people do not work.
weekend's.example: I hope this weekend's training will augment the navigation skills I learned on last term's expedition.

weeks.example: The whole campaign lasted just two busy weeks.

welcome.definition: a friendly greeting given to someone arriving, or to greet someone in a friendly way.
welcome.example: Please welcome our guest, the education officer, Adam!

welcoming.definition: friendly and pleasant towards people who are arriving or new.
welcoming.example: A warm, welcoming atmosphere filled the square that evening.

well'.definition: in a good, correct or thorough manner; skilfully or satisfactorily.
well'.example: Does repetition of the phrase 'buy less, choose well' make the campaign stronger or annoying?

went.definition: moved from one place to another, or, of a piece of writing, was sent to be printed or published.
went.example: The crowd went silent when Kofi raised his hand.

wetland.definition: an area of land that is always wet or covered with water, such as a marsh or swamp.
wetland.example: The school established new rules to protect the nearby wetland.

wetlands.definition: regions of low-lying land that are permanently wet or flooded, such as marshes.
wetlands.example: Is there a significant risk of flooding if the wetlands upstream continue to disappear?

whatever.definition: anything at all, no matter what; used to say something is true in every circumstance.
whatever.example: "Never forsake your walking partner in the hills," the guide told us, "whatever the weather does."

wheelchair.definition: a chair with wheels used by people who cannot walk, to help them move around.
wheelchair.example: I never realised how vulnerable pedestrians felt on our street until I pushed my brother's wheelchair.

whenever.definition: at any or every time that something happens.
whenever.example: The old wooden chair creaked whenever Ayeeyo leaned back.

whispered.definition: spoke very quietly and softly, often to avoid being overheard.
whispered.example: "Deforestation," Amal whispered to her friend Nora.

whole.definition: complete and entire; containing all the parts of something.
whole.example: We were almost late for the whole ceremony!

wilderness.definition: a wild, natural area of land that has not been changed or developed by people.
wilderness.example: Would you willingly relinquish your phone for a week to experience the wilderness without distractions?

wildfire.definition: a large, uncontrolled fire that spreads quickly, especially in a forest or dry area.

wildflower.definition: a flower that grows naturally in the wild, without being planted or cared for by people.
wildflower.example: It would devastate me to return next summer and find the wildflower meadow buried under concrete.

wildlife.definition: wild animals and plants living in their natural environment.
wildlife.example: Litter along the trail can wash into the river and harm wildlife.

willing.definition: ready and happy to do something without needing to be persuaded.
willing.example: I have learnt that good ideas soon attract people willing to help.

willingly.definition: happily and without needing to be forced or persuaded.
willingly.example: Would you willingly relinquish your phone for a week to experience the wilderness without distractions?

win.definition: to be the most successful in a competition, game or contest.
win.example: A true competitor never uses an unfair advantage to win.

wind.definition: the natural movement of air, especially a current of air blowing from one place to another.
wind.example: A cold wind blows down from the north during winter.

winger.definition: a player in a team sport, such as football, who plays on the side of the pitch.
winger.example: The coach drew arrows on the whiteboard to illustrate how the winger should cut inside.

winner.definition: the person or team that is most successful in a competition or contest.
winner.example: Nadir polished the trophy before handing it to the winner.

winning.definition: being the most successful in a competition or contest.
winning.example: How committed she was to winning that competition!

wins.definition: is the most successful in a competition, game or contest.
wins.example: Sound reasoning, not volume, is what wins a real debate.

winter.definition: the coldest season of the year, between autumn and spring.
winter.example: Have you outgrown that old winter coat yet?

wise.definition: having or showing good judgement, based on knowledge and experience.
wise.example: What wise advice Jamal's father gave about staying calm and choosing peace!

wisely.definition: in a sensible way that shows good judgement.
wisely.example: A busy schedule taught Imani how to manage her time wisely.

wish.definition: a desire or hope for something to happen, or to want something to happen.
wish.example: The seven symbolic items on the table each represented a different wish.

witness.definition: a person who sees an event happen, especially a crime or accident, or to see something happen.
witness.example: A dependable witness gives the same account every time she is asked.

witnessed.definition: saw something happen, especially an event or incident.
witnessed.example: Looking back, the most benevolent act I witnessed this year was quiet and completely unrewarded.

woman.example: Zane married a woman named Alina from a farming family inland.

won.definition: was successful in a competition or contest, finishing ahead of everyone else.
won.example: What was the essay titled that won first prize?

wonder.definition: to feel curious about something and want to know more.
wonder.example: Jamal began to wonder what was hidden behind Kofi's rough mask.

wonderfully.definition: in a way that is extremely good, impressive or pleasing.
wonderfully.example: What a wonderfully diverse set of voices, Maya!

wooden.example: Kofi kicked hard, and the wooden post finally gave way!

words.definition: units of language that carry meaning, spoken or written.
words.example: Can silence really be louder than words, do you think?

workable.definition: practical and likely to succeed if used or carried out.
workable.example: The design team took a whole weekend to conceive a workable plan for the recycling app.

worked.definition: did a job or task, or, of a plan or machine, functioned successfully.
worked.example: The women worked so hard, Leo!

worker.definition: a person who does a job, especially one involving physical or practical effort.
worker.example: The play's central dialogue between a shopper and a factory worker silenced the entire audience.

workers.definition: people who do jobs, especially involving physical or practical effort.
workers.example: The factory employs workers from towns all along the coast.

workers'.definition: belonging to people who do jobs, especially involving physical or practical effort.
workers'.example: Is calling the factory a beehive a fair metaphor, or does it hide the workers' exhaustion?

working.definition: doing a job or task, or, of a machine or method, functioning correctly.
working.example: Local farmers are working to reverse decades of deforestation.

workload.definition: the amount of tasks or effort that a person or machine has to complete.
workload.example: Does technology genuinely ease our workload, or does it simply add new kinds of tasks?

works.definition: functions or operates as intended, or does a job.
works.example: Have you ever visited the hospital where Sana works?

workshop.definition: a room or building where things are made or repaired using tools, or a session where people learn a skill through practical activity.
workshop.example: The workshop buzzed with activity, didn't it?

world.definition: the earth, along with all its countries, peoples and natural features.
world.example: Never hide your light, Samira, the world needs it!

worry.definition: to feel anxious or troubled about something that might happen.
worry.example: Ben's voice broke with worry as he described the fire.

worse.definition: More bad than something else; of lower quality.
worse.example: Just walk away, Kofi, before this gets any worse!

worsens.definition: becomes more severe, serious or unpleasant than before.
worsens.example: "Grandfather's chronic knee pain worsens in winter," said Maya, "so we visit him more often then."

worth.definition: having a particular value, especially in money, or deserving something.
worth.example: Every family carries stories that are worth remembering.

worthless.definition: having no real value, use or importance.
worthless.example: Is ambition worthless without the discipline to work towards it every single day?

worthwhile.definition: important, valuable or rewarding enough to justify the time or effort spent on it.
worthwhile.example: "Every worthwhile endeavour begins badly," our teacher joked, holding up her own messy first draft.

wound.definition: moved in a series of curves or bends, following a twisting course.
wound.example: A narrow path wound through the forest towards the river.

woven.definition: made by crossing threads, strips or strands over and under each other to form a fabric, basket or similar object.
woven.example: Where did you buy that woven mat, Amal?

wrapped.definition: covered something completely by folding paper, cloth or another material around it.
wrapped.example: Jamal wrapped a bandage around Kofi's scratched arm.

wrapping.definition: covering something completely by folding paper, cloth or another material around it.
wrapping.example: 'Warm soup will alleviate the shivering,' said the first-aider, wrapping a blanket around the soaked hiker.

wristbands.definition: bands worn around the wrist, often to show that someone has paid to enter an event.
wristbands.example: I felt proud staying vigilant at the gate, checking wristbands while my friends enjoyed the show.

writer.definition: a person whose job or skill is producing books, articles or other texts.
writer.example: Plagiarising a script is unfair to the writer who created it.

writer's.definition: belonging to a person whose job or skill is producing texts such as books or articles.
writer's.example: A loyal reader notices when a writer's voice starts to change.

writers.definition: people whose job or skill is producing books, articles or other texts.
writers.example: What a brilliant idea, starting a journal for young writers!

writes.definition: produces text by forming letters or words on a surface, such as paper or a screen.
writes.example: Maya writes down every story her grandmother tells her.

writing.definition: the activity of forming letters or words to communicate, or a piece of text produced this way.
writing.example: Her writing overflowed with metaphors, didn't it?

written.definition: produced in the form of letters or words on a page or screen, rather than spoken.
written.example: What useful details are written below the main report!

wrong.definition: not correct, or not morally right.
wrong.example: Zara, you tapped my shoulder, what's wrong?

wrongdoing.example: A fair leader tries to punish wrongdoing without being unnecessarily cruel.

wrongly.definition: in a way that is incorrect or unfair.
wrongly.example: The security footage exonerated the caretaker, who had been wrongly blamed for the missing tablets.

wrote.definition: communicated something by putting words down in a letter, message or other piece of writing, at a time in the past
wrote.example: Who actually wrote this new policy, Sir?

year.definition: a period of twelve months, used to measure how long something lasts or when it happens
year.example: Kofi and Milo were rivals just a year ago.

year's.definition: belonging to, or taking place within, a particular twelve-month period
year's.example: Was last year's festival bigger than this one?

yearly.definition: happening once every twelve months, on a regular schedule
yearly.example: Should the geography syllabus incorporate a yearly field trip to the wetland reserve?

years.definition: periods of twelve months, used to describe a long stretch of time
years.example: Why do doctors need so many years of training?

young.definition: having lived or existed for only a short time; not old
young.example: What a capable young engineer Tariq has become!

younger.definition: having lived for a shorter time than someone else, especially within the same family
younger.example: The younger children love to play near the old field.

youngest.definition: having lived for the shortest time among a group of people, especially siblings
youngest.example: Only twelve years separated Nadir from his youngest sister.

youth.definition: young people thought of as a group, especially teenagers and those in their early twenties
youth.example: I've just started a youth podcast, and I'd love a guest like you.

zealous.definition: Very enthusiastic and eager about something.
zealous.example: I am zealous about protecting our old festival recipes, copying each one into a notebook.

zone.definition: a particular area or section of a place, marked out because it has a special purpose or feature
zone.example: I was oblivious to how loud our street was until I visited the new quiet zone.

zoo.definition: a place where various kinds of wild animals are kept so the public can see them
